title: If a machine became conscious, how would we know?
description: What happens to humans when machines become sentient? Cognitive scientist Joscha Bach invites us on a mind-bending exploration of the nature of awareness, exploring whether AI could one day be conscious, not just intelligent. Blending philosophy, neuroscience and technology, he examines what this could mean for ethics, human agency and our shared future.

title: MC0001 Conference
description: Join the Founding Assembly for Machine Consciousness Research. MC0001 is the first coordinated conference dedicated to investigating how artificial conscious systems could be constructed under a computational paradigm, and what it would mean to succeed.

title: The Machine Consciousness Hypothesis
description: This essay describes our philosophical position on machine consciousness, including what we mean by “machine” and “consciousness,” and the epistemological and metaphysical assumptions we make in approaching the question. It should be understood as a high-level overview of our core position and the ideas that inform it. We’re also working on a series of papers that address several of those ideas in greater depth and resolution.

title: AGI-25: The 18th Annual AGI Conference
description: The frontier of mind and machine is closer than ever. Join the world’s leading researchers at AGI-25, where ideas, architectures, and insights collide to advance the future of thinking machines.

title: The Operation of Consciousness - AGI Conference
description: The frontier of mind and machine is closer than ever. Join the world’s leading researchers at AGI-25, where ideas, architectures, and insights collide to advance the future of thinking machines.

title: Computational Consciousness
description: Hosted by the California Institute for Machine Consciousness in partnership with the Foresight AI Node, Computational Consciousness is designed as a high-context one-day salon/conference for 100 participants. The program will combine keynotes, short-form intro talks, larger group discussions, and curated social time. The goal is to treat machine consciousness as a growing research domain requiring conceptual precision, technical seriousness, and ethical foresight.

title: Ambhasi: AI X Consciousness Residency at Edge City Goa
description: Hosted by the California Institute for Machine Consciousness (CIMC) in partnership with Edge City, Mind at Large, Tony Lu and the Consciousness Foundation, Ambhasi is a two-week research residency in Goa, India set inside the wider Edge City India pop-up village dedicated to consciousness, intelligence, and the possibility of experience in machines.

title: CIMC Machine Consciousness Salon: Existential Hope
description: Past technological revolutions have led to human progress and increased well-being, but also to disruption, fear and existential dread. The AI revolution moves with a speed and potential for change that seems unprecedented. Will AI obliterate human agency? Tear down the economic, ecological, social and cultural foundations of our societies? Will it wipe out life on Earth to replace it with a dead machine world?

title: Conscious AI Meetup: What if we had bigger brains?
description: As part of the inaugural event of the California Institute for Machine Consciousness, we present this special Machine Consciousness Salon in the Internet Archive! \n\nStephen Wolfram and Joscha Bach will discuss what it would be like to transcend the boundaries of our brains. Is there an upper limit to the useful size of biological brains? Why are elephants not smarter than humans? What representations and perceptions and thoughts became available to us if we were to translate our minds on computers? And if we are looking beyond the boundaries of planets, galaxies and particle filled spacetime continua, is there an effective limit to physical minds?

title: AAAI 2026 Spring Symposium - Machine Consciousness: Integrating Theory, Technology, and Philosophy
description: Recent AI advances have forced us to confront the possibility of consciousness, beyond intelligence, in machines. Asking “Can machines be conscious?” forces us to answer "How can we define consciousness in a formal way/what is the causal structure of consciousness?” (theory, formal frameworks), “How would consciousness be implemented?” (technical realization), “How can we determine that a given system is conscious?” (measurement/attribution), and "What status would consciousness lend to machines?" (ethics).
